title: Scenario
description: A scenario picks profiles and settings. Seeds are neutral integers, never date-shaped. S1b adds fields additively.

feedback.description: L5 feeds back into L1 (experiment 2). Absent means false; S1 builds only the open loop.

raw_layer.description: The raw device layer of ADR-0014 (spec section 2.4). Absent means false: every earlier scenario keeps a byte-identical event log. Not one of the ten flags.

capture_path.description: Overrides the capture path of every preset (spec section 5, 'Capture path'). Read only with raw_layer true; with the layer off a scenario that sets it fails validation, because a silent no-op would mislead.

export_schedule.description: When an analyzer export reaches the host (A216; the staffed window is A098, spec section 2.4.2): at the end of each staffed window (window_end, the default) or at the instant each result is produced (per_run). Needs raw_layer true. A capture-path contrast holds it fixed so that only the path changes.

controller_log_cut.description: How a controller cuts its log files (A217): one file per record type per day (daily, the default; the file reaches the host at the end of its day) or each row as written (per_row; the row reaches the host at its own stamp). Needs raw_layer true. A capture-path contrast holds it fixed so that only the path changes.

bay_controllers.description: The controller profile of each bay, bay 1 first (spec section 2.4.2: a bay uses one controller profile; the default raw-layer scenario puts one bay on each family). Needs raw_layer true. Absent: no controller log is emitted and the layer stays analyzer-side only.

bay_profiles.description: The bioreactor profile of each bay, bay 1 first (ADR-0015, spec section 4.5.2). The length is the number of bays, reactor_count over bay_size rounded up. Absent: every bay takes profiles.bioreactor.

analyzer_profiles.description: The analyzer profile of each analyzer, analyzer 1 first (ADR-0015, spec section 4.5.2). The length is analyzer_count. Absent: every analyzer takes profiles.analyzer. An analyte has one profile in a fleet (spec section 4.5.4, rule B).

calendar_anchor.description: The synthetic calendar date of scenario second 0 (a Monday, spec section 2.1), as YYYY-MM-DD; the emitters turn integer seconds into wall-clock text from it. Needs raw_layer true.

breakout.description: One scripted break-out event (spec 11.4, 11.8; ADR-0013): a hidden contamination with an origin, the shared lots and equipment, the scripted response and the confirming samples. Absent means no event: every earlier scenario keeps a byte-identical event log. Every instant and delay is in hours from scenario start; every number is {value, unit, ref}. `lag` is the time from the onset to the first signal (A139) and `ramp` the length of the linear signal ramp that ends at it (A141), both in hours; absent, the profile's values apply, and the ramp may not exceed the lag. The delays of `response` (A176), the topology (A177) and the inputs the event-type profile names (for the bacterial profile the bioburden volume, A225; for the mycoplasma profile A219 to A224 and A226) have no default and are required: a scenario that omits one is refused, naming it.

profile.description: The event-type profile under scenarios/profiles/breakout/ (for example bacterial); data, never branched on by id.

origin.description: Where the contamination enters (spec 11.4 origins, 11.8.2 rule S1). seed_lot and medium_lot name a declared lot, shared_equipment a declared item; contaminated_at is the hidden instant from which the item is contaminated. unit_equipment is a unit's own equipment, with a scenario instant. sampling names the draw (a sample id) after which the organism enters the unit.

topology.description: A177 (widened to equipment): which units consume which lot or use which equipment item, and when. A seed lot is consumed at the inoculation of its unit (no `at`); a medium lot and an equipment use carry `at`. A unit has at most one seed lot. A consumption or use at or after the end of its unit (a stop or a harvest) leaves no record.

response.description: A176, the two delays, both required with no default and identical across architectures: from the first signal to the scripted response (the stop of each affected unit and the confirming draws), and from a positive result to the hold or quarantine action.

confirm.description: The units that get one confirming sample at the first decision instant (11.8.2 rule S2).

inputs.description: The scenario inputs the profile declares and gives no default (for the bacterial profile bioburden_sample_volume_ml, A225; for the mycoplasma profile the DO rise ramp A219, the plateau and viability-fall delays and multipliers A220 to A223, the nucleic-acid target A224 and its sample volume A226). A profile that names its ramp as an input (ramp_input) takes the ramp from here and refuses the `ramp` field.
